core_obligations: Set up the coordinates: with u_x sending x to [e1], write v = sum_i v_x^{(i)} e_{i,x} in the eigenbasis e_{i,x} = u_x^{-1} e_i and record the labelled equation (gtv) giving the diagonal action g_t^x v = (e^{-t}v_x^{(1)}, v_x^{(2)}, ..., e^t v_x^{(d)}) (proof lines 292-307).

First direction: assuming d(x,v) <= H(v)^{-beta} along arbitrarily large rational points, expand F(v) = 0 as 2v_x^{(1)}v_x^{(d)} + G(v_x^{(2)},...,v_x^{(d-1)}) = 0, bound |v_x^{(d)}| << ||v||^{-2beta+1}, choose t with e^t = ||v||^beta and conclude from (gtv) that ||g_t^x v|| << e^{-(1-1/beta)t}, i.e. gamma(x) >= 1 - 1/beta(x) (proof lines 308-322).

Converse direction: assuming ||g_t^x v|| <= e^{-gamma t}, use F(v) = F(g_t^x v) bounded by e^{-gamma t} < 1 to force F(v) = 0, so v is a rational point of X; bound |v_x^{(1)}| <= e^{(1-gamma)t}, |v_x^{(d)}| <= e^{-(1+gamma)t} and the middle coordinates through (gtv), get d(x,v) << ||v||^{-1/(1-gamma)}, i.e. beta(x) >= 1/(1-gamma(x)) (proof lines 324-328).
Combine the two inequalities into the equality beta(x) = 1/(1 - gamma(x)) (proof lines 322 and 328).
proof_roadmap: Fix the eigenbasis e_{i,x} = u_x^{-1} e_i and record the diagonal action (gtv) (proof lines 292-307).
Approximation-to-escape: F(v) = 0 bounds |v_x^{(d)}| by ||v||^{-2beta+1}; with e^t = ||v||^beta the orbit contracts at rate 1 - 1/beta (proof lines 308-322).
Escape-to-approximation: F(v) = F(g_t^x v) forces F(v) = 0; the coordinate bounds through (gtv) give d(x,v) << ||v||^{-1/(1-gamma)} (proof lines 324-327).
Conclude beta(x) = 1/(1 - gamma(x)) (proof lines 322 and 328).

The result is the paper's basic tool linking the diophantine exponent to homogeneous dynamics, used for the Dirichlet principle in Section 2 and the exponent computations of Sections 5-6. H3.

statement_spans.label: author theorem environment with its own label drapeau; statement at source lines 368-378, printed as Theorem 3.3 in the journal: for a diagonal flow (a_t) in GL_d(R) and an algebraic lattice Delta in R^d, the limits Lambda_i = lim (1/t) log lambda_i(a_t Delta) exist for every i, and if the indices are grouped into equal-exponent blocks i_1 < ... < i_s then there exists a partial flag 0 = T_0 < T_1 < ... < T_{s+1} = R^d of Delta-rational subspaces such that dim T_l = i_l and, for all large t, a_t T_l contains the first i_l successive minima of a_t Delta

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof, explicitly titled 'Demonstration du theoreme drapeau': setting Lambda_i as the liminf, defining the index blocks, and proving by induction on k in {0,...,s} the existence of the partial flag with the three listed properties -- for the inductive step, a sequence (t_n) realizing Lambda_{i_k} with eps = (1/3)(Lambda_{i_k+1} - Lambda_{i_k}) and the strong subspace theorem produce a Delta-rational T_k of dimension i_k carrying the first i_k minima along a subsequence; the covolume estimate covol <= exp[t sum (i_l - i_{l-1}) Lambda_{i_l} + o(t)] gives tau(T_k) <= sum (i_l - i_{l-1}) Lambda_{i_l}, hence the numbered inequality ikmoins (tau(T_k) - tau(T_{k-1}))/(i_k - i_{k-1}) <= Lambda_{i_k}; Minkowski's second theorem applied in a_t T_k bounds the middle minima by exp[t(tau(T_k) - tau(T_{k-1})) + o(t)], which combined with ikmoins forces Lambda_i = (tau(T_k) - tau(T_{k-1}))/(i_k - i_{k-1}) on each block; the final norm-separation argument (vectors outside a_t T_k have norm above e^{t(Lambda_{i_k} + 2 eps)}) shows the first i_k minima are attained in a_t T_k for all large t (source lines 409-459)

metadata.title: Uniform exponent of rational points on rational quadrics: the Roth-type formula beta(x) = 1 + 1/k_x

statement_spans.label: author theorem environment with its own label roth_quadrique (Exposant d'un point algebrique); statement at source lines 176-182, printed as Theorem 1.2 in the journal: for a rational quadric X in P^{d-1} and a rational point x in X(Q) contained in no totally isotropic rational projective subspace, the uniform exponent beta(x) equals 1; more generally beta(x) = 1 + 1/k_x where k_x is the minimal dimension of a totally isotropic rational projective subspace containing x (k_x = +infinity by convention when none exists)

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof, explicitly titled 'Demonstration du theoreme roth_quadrique': the lower bound beta(x) >= 1 comes from the corollary dirichlet (journal 2.2) and the Dirichlet drawer principle inside any totally isotropic rational subspace W containing x gives beta(x) >= 1 + 1/dim W, so it remains to prove the reverse inequality; if x lies in ker F then all very good approximations lie in ker F and beta(x) is the classical Schmidt exponent in that projective plane (cite schmidt_da, Corollary 1C); otherwise the proposition dani (journal 2.1) gives beta(x) = 1/(1 - gamma(x)) with gamma(x) the escape rate of g_t^x Z^d, and the theorem drapeau (journal 3.3) produces a rank-i_1 sublattice T_1 carrying the first minima with the numbered two-sided estimate kfirst e^{t(tau(T_1)/i_1 - eps)} <= lambda_1 <= ... <= lambda_{i_1} <= e^{t(tau(T_1)/i_1 + eps)}; since a_t = diag(e^{-t}, 1, ..., 1, e^t) the rate tau(T_1) is 0 or -1: if 0 then gamma(x) = 0 and beta(x) = 1 (and x lies in no rational isotropic subspace, so k_x = +infinity); if -1 then gamma(x) = 1/i_1 and beta(x) = 1 + 1/(i_1 - 1), and the rationality of F forces F(u_i, u_j) = 0 for large t (bounded denominator argument), so T_1 is totally isotropic and contains the direction of x, whence k_x <= i_1 - 1 and beta(x) = 1 + 1/(i_1 - 1) <= 1 + 1/k_x (source lines 463-481)
